sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the strongest driver of predicted default, accounting for about 37% of the model's importance, and its effect is mostly increasing: risk stays low until utilization passes roughly 0.72 and then rises sharply.
Past delinquencies are the second most important driver, and risk increases with their number, mainly from having none to having at least one.
Higher income is associated with lower predicted risk, though its effect is moderate and concentrated in the step around 54,200 dollars.
Length of credit history has only a weak effect, with longer histories associated with somewhat lower risk.
The data do not settle whether the debt-to-income ratio has any consistent effect on risk.
Application attributes such as age, the two standardised features and recent credit inquiries hardly matter.
The effect of utilization is larger when there are past delinquencies, though this interaction is modest.
Utilization does not meaningfully interact with credit history length, and income and delinquencies do not interact in a way of practical size.
